content.text: If your scalp is flaky and irritated, it is likely more than just #dryscalp. This is something called #seborrheicdermatitis. The last thing you want to do is add oils to the scalp as this can worsen the condition. Instead try treating with shampoos which contain active ingredients like zinc pyrothione, ketoconazole and selenium sulfide. Otherwise go see your #dermatologist for prescription stregnth treatments.

Stop putting thick hair oils on your flaky scalp! 🛑🧴 If you have thick, yellowish, oily crusts on your scalp that itch intensely, it is NOT dry skin. It is Scalp Seborrheic Dermatitis—a reaction to an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast. This yeast feeds on oil! If you apply coconut, castor, or rosemary oil to fix the "dryness," you are just feeding the yeast and making the crusts thicker! 🧬 Welcome to Day 1/30 of clearing every type of stubborn skin texture! Here is your foolproof, dermatologist-approved scalp rescue squad: 🧪 STEP 1 (The Neutralizer): Do NOT scratch the scales off—you will pull your hair out! Use a Salicylic Acid scalp serum to chemically unbind the dead skin from your follicles safely. 🧼 STEP 2 (The Halter): Wash your roots with a medicated shampoo containing Ketoconazole or Zinc Pyrithione. This starves the yeast and stops the overproduction of oily scales. 🌿 STEP 3 (The Soother): Seborrheic Dermatitis causes severe inflammation. Apply a lightweight, oil-free soothing serum like Centella or Aloe to instantly calm the red, angry skin barrier. 📌 SAVE this safe scalp rescue routine. What texture should we fix next?
